question: Where is medication placed when using the sublingual route?
explanation: Sublingual medications are placed specifically beneath the tongue for rapid dissolution and absorption. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h1)

question: Why is the sublingual route often chosen during a medical emergency?

options.A: It releases medicine slowly over twenty-four hours.
options.B: It prevents the patient from accidentally choking.
options.C: It allows the drug to enter the bloodstream very quickly.
options.D: It tastes much better than swallowed pills.

explanation: Rapid absorption bypasses digestion, providing fast symptom relief when every second counts. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h1)

question: Blood from under the tongue flows directly into which major vein on its way to the heart?
explanation: You've got this! The sublingual veins drain straight into the internal jugular vein to reach the heart quickly. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h2)

question: What process does a sublingual drug successfully avoid by entering the bloodstream directly?
explanation: Great job! Because it skips the liver's initial breakdown (first-pass metabolism), more active drug reaches your patient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h3)

question: What does high bioavailability mean for a medication?

options.A: The drug stays active in the body for many days.
options.B: A large amount of the active drug reaches the bloodstream.
options.C: The medication dissolves very slowly in cold water.
options.D: It is completely safe from causing any side effects.

explanation: High bioavailability means more of the active medicine is available to do its job in the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary advantage of the sublingual route?
explanation: Direct absorption into blood vessels gives sublingual medicines a very fast therapeutic effect. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h4)

question: A patient becomes dizzy and nauseated shortly after taking a sublingual tablet. What unique advantage of this route can the nurse utilize?

options.A: Give a large glass of milk to neutralize the medicine.
options.B: Instruct the patient to spit out any remaining undissolved medication.
options.C: Wait for the liver to filter out the toxic portion.
options.D: Pump the patient's stomach immediately to remove the drug.

explanation: Because absorption happens in the mouth, removing unabsorbed medication can stop further entry into the blood. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h4)

question: What usually happens if a patient accidentally swallows a sublingual tablet with water?

options.A: The drug will turn into a toxic substance in the intestines.
options.B: The drug may be destroyed by stomach acid and liver enzymes.
options.C: There will be no change in how the drug works.
options.D: The drug will absorb twice as fast through the stomach lining.

explanation: Correct! Swallowing it means it faces stomach acid and the liver, which can weaken or destroy the drug before it works. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h5)

question: Why is the sublingual route unsuitable for medications that require a large dose?

options.A: Large doses dissolve too quickly to be safe.
options.B: Large amounts will stain the teeth permanently.
options.C: Big pills cause the tongue to become paralyzed.
options.D: The physical space under the tongue is very small.

explanation: Only small, highly potent doses fit comfortably under the tongue for effective mucosal absorption. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h5)

question: What is the most common medication given sublingually for sudden chest pain?
explanation: Nitroglycerin is the classic sublingual drug used to rapidly dilate coronary vessels during angina. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h6)

question: What shared feature do all standard sublingual medications possess?

options.A: They require digestion in the small intestine.
options.B: They take at least two hours to start working.
options.C: They must be mixed with thick syrup first.
options.D: They are potent in very small doses.

explanation: Because the sublingual space is limited, only drugs that work in tiny amounts are given this way. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h6)

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient right after placing a sublingual tablet?

options.A: Drink a full glass of water immediately to wash it down.
options.B: Lie flat on your back for at least one hour.
options.C: Do not eat, drink, or smoke until the pill is fully dissolved.
options.D: Chew the tablet quickly to help it enter the bloodstream.

explanation: Eating or drinking washes the medication away before it can absorb through the oral mucosa. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h7)

question: Why must sublingual nitroglycerin tablets be stored in a special dark, airtight glass bottle?

options.A: Glass containers prevent the pills from melting in warm weather.
options.B: Light turns the medication into a dangerous poison.
options.C: The medication loses potency easily when exposed to light and air.
options.D: Dark bottles keep the tablets from sticking together.

explanation: Spot on! Nitroglycerin loses its strength quickly if light and air get to it, so the special bottle keeps it potent. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h7)
